html:
SMTO-SCH-0003 — That time is skipped or repeated by a clock change

GUID: d53123f1-1f84-4458-b70c-c8cfa5c29e00
Slug: schedule-local-time-is-ambiguous-or-nonexistent-supply
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: sch

What happened

  • On the day you picked, the clocks change for daylight saving time, so that exact time either doesn't happen or happens twice. SMTO didn't save the schedule because it couldn't tell which moment you meant.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In the schedule's At field, choose a time outside the clock-change hour, for example 3:30 AM instead of 2:30 AM. Clock changes usually happen in the early morning, so a time outside that hour happens exactly once.
  2. Or choose a different date for the first run, then save again. Only the day of the clock change has the missing or repeated hour.
  3. If you asked SMTO in a message, ask again and include the time-zone offset, for example "2:30 AM UTC-07:00". An offset names one exact moment, so SMTO doesn't have to guess.
  4. Before saving, read the summary line under the schedule settings and check the date and time it shows. It shows when SMTO will run the schedule, so you can confirm it matches what you meant.

What success looks like

  • The schedule saves and its next run time on the Schedules page is the moment you intended.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, and mention the date, time and time zone you chose. Don't keep saving the same time; change the time first.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Schedule time resolution found that the naive local date-time maps to zero or two UTC instants in the schedule's time zone (a daylight-saving gap or overlap), so an explicit UTC offset is required.

What this means

  • The time-zone name was accepted, but this local wall-clock time does not identify exactly one instant. A clock change can skip a local time or repeat it. The error does not establish which case occurred, nor whether any previously saved schedule ran.

Why this can happen

  • Local time has zero or two valid UTC candidates in the selected zone.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the date and local time with that zone’s clock change. For a repeated time, select the intended UTC offset; for a skipped time, choose a real time outside the gap.

How to fix it

  • Supply next_run_at as an ISO date-time with an explicit UTC offset (for example -07:00 or -08:00) or choose a local time outside the DST transition; resolve_at in events/timing.py rejects naive wall times that map to zero or two instants. The error does not establish whether it was a gap or an overlap, nor whether any previously saved schedule ran.
  • Provide an ISO date and time with the intended explicit UTC offset, or choose an unambiguous local time. Check the resulting UTC instant before saving.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Schedule validation resolves one instant at the intended date, time and offset.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • A naive local datetime round-trips to zero or two UTC instants; this shared identity does not distinguish gap from overlap.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
